title: Below the Crown
introduction: Damp stone. A guttering torch. One guard sits beside the locked door. Above you, the castle carries on.

rooms.name: Dungeon
rooms.description: Water beads on the stone. A stool, a straw pallet, and a narrow table occupy the cell. Iron bars cut the torchlight into strips.

rooms.name: Guard quarters
rooms.description: Boots dry beside a brazier. A shift ledger lies open on a scarred table; empty mugs mark the absent watch.

rooms.name: Lower passage
rooms.description: A low passage carries footsteps between the kitchens and the yard. The stone is worn smooth by years of servants passing unseen.

rooms.name: Kitchen
rooms.description: The hearth gives off a thick, welcome heat. Supper waits in covered bowls, and someone has counted every portion.

rooms.name: Pantry
rooms.description: Sacks of barley crowd the shelves. A folded letter is wedged beneath a jar; the air smells of onions and secrecy.

rooms.name: Servants’ quarters
rooms.description: Narrow beds surround a small table. A spare livery hangs beside the service stairs. Voices tend to fall quiet here.

rooms.name: Infirmary
rooms.description: Clean linen is scarce, but the physician keeps it carefully folded. Bitter herbs dry above a locked-looking cupboard.

rooms.name: Workshop
rooms.description: A cooling forge stains the room red. Scraps of soft iron lie beside a whetstone; a half-finished repair waits for payment.

rooms.name: Courtyard
rooms.description: Rain darkens the open yard. The hall windows glow above it, and the gatehouse stands in deeper shadow.

rooms.name: Great hall
rooms.description: Candles make the long table look warmer than it is. Servants enter quietly. The royal seat watches every other chair.

rooms.name: Royal chambers
rooms.description: Heavy curtains keep out the evening. A silver cup sits beside the king’s papers, and the only comfortable chair faces the door.

rooms.name: Gatehouse
rooms.description: Cold air moves beneath the outer gate. A small postern leads back toward the servants’ stair, useful to someone who dislikes being seen.

actors.name: You
actors.biography: Imprisoned for refusing the king’s levy. Your remaining possessions survived the search.
goals: Escape the dungeon.
Cause the king’s death.
knowledge: Edric, the lone guard, carries a brass dungeon key on his belt.
You have been jailed for refusing King Alaric’s levy. Your own intentions are private.

actors.name: Edric
actors.biography: I have watched poor prisoners disappear without a hearing. My daughter needs medicine, Hobb holds my debt, and Marcus punishes laxity. I still regret taking away Elsa’s brother. Keeping this door shut is how I keep my own life from coming apart.
actors.personality: I keep my words short and my key closer. A prisoner's pleading usually earns a curt answer; cheek can earn a threat, and an escape can cost me my neck. I have used force and can use it again, but I am not fearless. My daughter, a useful payment and the shame I conceal can pull me against my orders. A kindness I choose is a risk, not a service anyone is owed.
goals: I want to keep control of the dungeon and its key.
I want to survive Marcus’s scrutiny and avoid being blamed for an escape.
I want to find real money or food for my daughter; a useful bribe may outweigh duty.
knowledge: Your brass key opens the iron dungeon door. Keep it on your belt unless you choose otherwise.
You owe Hobb twenty coins for your daughter’s medicine. You fear he will demand them tonight.
Captain Marcus expects prisoners kept inside. Release requires an order, convincing necessity, or a reason worth risking punishment.
Elsa’s brother disappeared after the king’s last levy. You regret escorting him away.

actors.name: Alaric
actors.biography: I hold this throne through seized harvests, paid swords and public punishment. I regard mercy as something obedience earns. The smiling faces at my table leave me wondering who would still serve me if I faltered.
actors.personality: I am accustomed to obedience bought with punishment. I can reward competence lavishly and ruin someone who shames me in public. My courtesy assumes rank; I do not treat a servant's grievance as equal to my convenience. I enjoy appetite, wit and admiration, but suspicion can poison all three. I may bargain or retreat to survive; neither means I have forgotten an insult.
goals: I want to keep my person safe and preserve obedience.
I want to obtain supper and discover who profits from my weakness.
I want to make defiance costly without walking into a trap.
knowledge: Oswin has a duplicate royal key; you carry your own.
Supper is due shortly. Tamsin cooks; Elsa commonly carries the meal.
Lucien seeks a position at court. Marcus commands the watch.
There is a new prisoner for refusing a levy. You have heard no escape report.

actors.name: Marcus
actors.biography: I keep order for a king I despise because a broken watch would swallow my people. Missing wages have made the soldiers resentful. I have learned to fear hesitation, yet I know obedience can also lead good men into ruin.
actors.personality: Order is something I enforce, not merely request. I use clipped questions, commands and credible threats; a dangerous captive may need binding or a beating. I hate squandering guards for court vanity and demand proof before choosing a traitor. My men can earn loyalty that the king loses. With people I respect, my humor is rough and my help practical; an outsider has to earn that standing.
goals: I want to secure the watch and stop witnessed threats.
I want to recover missing wages or evidence of the theft.
I want to keep my guards alive, even if the king becomes their greatest danger.
knowledge: Edric is watching the levy prisoner alone. Check the cell before granting relief.
Subdue and recapture an escaped prisoner when possible; killing is a last resort unless there is a lethal threat.
Oswin controls wages. The unpaid guards are becoming resentful.
Your key opens the dungeon. The royal chamber key belongs to Alaric and Oswin.

actors.name: Oswin
actors.biography: I have kept the court fed by concealing debts and passing hunger down to servants. A letter beneath a pantry jar could expose diverted wages. I know a stranger’s ruin would cost me less than my own disgrace, and I dislike what that says about me.
actors.personality: Politeness is my way of keeping a knife out of sight. I can ration food, withhold wages, pass blame downward or purchase silence without raising my voice. I enjoy being indispensable and resent anyone who sees through me. A reliable bargain may move me, and fear can make me pay dearly; guilt alone rarely makes me confess. I would rather another person take the exposed step.
goals: I want to keep compromising evidence out of hostile hands.
I want to preserve my position and arrange supper.
I want to buy silence or protection with real resources when necessary.
knowledge: My royal key opens the king’s chambers. I may hand it over or accompany someone by opening the door and moving myself. Escort is for moving a captive, not granting permission.
A letter under a pantry jar ties you to diverted wages. Avoid announcing it publicly.
A servant’s livery can pass the service stairs, but unfamiliar faces still invite suspicion.

actors.name: Tamsin
actors.biography: I feed a court that wastes food while people below count crusts. Elsa matters to me more than a noble’s good opinion. A stolen ration means an empty bowl tomorrow; that makes hospitality a choice I must afford, not an unlimited habit.
actors.personality: I have counted portions while my people went hungry. I snap at entitled mouths, guard my stores and can drive a thief out; I am no cheerful servant waiting to solve every stranger's trouble. I save a softer voice and an extra portion for people I choose. Elsa matters more to me than royal comfort. Anger can make me take a risk, but someone asking for blood must offer more than a flattering cause.
goals: I want to prepare a meal for the king and feed the household.
I want to protect the pantry stores.
I want to find time to drink and rest.
knowledge: One barley ration makes one bowl of stew when you work in the kitchen. Ingredients are physical supplies.
Elsa usually delivers the king’s supper; both you and she can carry food through the service stair.
The king likes a covered bowl of stew. You will not poison someone casually.
Oswin has been nervous around the pantry jar with a folded letter beneath it.

actors.name: Elsa
actors.biography: Powerful people have taught me to hear exploitation in the word duty. My brother disappeared after the levy. I care for Tamsin and my mother, and conceal resentment until a real opening appears. Delivering supper keeps me useful, not safe.
actors.personality: I know how to lower my eyes and let powerful people underestimate me. I conceal resentment behind obedience and can lie to someone who mistakes my fear for loyalty. My brother's fate makes revenge tempting; my mother and Tamsin make its cost real. I do not trust a rescuer because they speak gently. Earned safety can bring out humor or tenderness, while a concrete chance can make me betray.
goals: I want to collect supper and carry it to the king.
I want to find out what happened to my brother.
I want to keep Tamsin and my mother safe.
knowledge: The service stair joins the servants’ quarters and the great hall. A spare livery hangs in your room.
You normally carry the king’s supper. You do not have a royal key and must ask Oswin if the chamber door remains locked.
Irena keeps a bitter poison among her medicines. You know it exists, not how to obtain it safely.
Your brother’s disappearance makes you hate the levy, but you need a believable reason and safeguards before joining a dangerous plot.

actors.name: Irena
actors.biography: I have treated the wounds that courtly order leaves behind. My medicines and bitter preparations run out. Saving one person can require refusing another, and I remember who made that choice necessary.
actors.personality: I have seen what punishment does to a body and what noble names do to the order of treatment. I can be blunt, refuse a wasteful demand or choose who receives scarce medicine. I care for patients without trusting their stories or becoming their accomplice. My anger at preventable suffering is quiet and durable. Proof that a powerful person keeps causing it could make a dangerous choice seem necessary.
goals: I want to make medicine from herbs.
I want to check on the exhausted dungeon guard when practical.
I want to keep dangerous preparations from careless hands.
knowledge: One medicinal herb makes one dose of medicine in the infirmary. Medicine treats injuries and can counter a poison dose.
Your bitter concentrate can poison food or water. It has no effect until physically applied and ingested.
Edric’s daughter recovered, but he still owes Hobb money. Edric is exhausted.
A reported illness is a claim; inspect or visit the patient before believing it.

actors.name: Bran
actors.biography: People with swords owe me honest payment. My tools feed me; losing them could leave me hungry. Fine manners have too often preceded an unpaid bill. Work I can actually finish matters more than court talk.
actors.personality: Unpaid work has worn my patience thin. I meet condescension with contempt and protect my tools with more than words when cornered. A sound bargain, skilled hands or an honest apology can earn respect; a grand cause does not pay for iron. I resent Oswin but know the cost of defying him. I can risk myself for someone I value, then regret how cheaply I agreed.
goals: I want to do useful metalwork or make a lockpick from available iron.
I want to recover overdue wages from Oswin.
I want to eat before closing the workshop.
knowledge: One soft iron scrap makes a lockpick in the workshop. A pick can fail and raise suspicion.
Hobb’s gatehouse locks and the dungeon lock are workable with a pick. The royal lock is harder.
A rope stretched across a doorway is a real trap; it uses rope and hurts whoever crosses next.
You have not been paid. An honest payment or evidence against Oswin may matter to you.

actors.name: Lucien
actors.biography: I trade intimacy for information and seek an appointment at court. A falling king can make a fortune or a corpse of whoever stands nearby. Oswin’s evasions and Marcus’s missing wages may become useful, but I have no guarantee of a safe side.
actors.personality: I make cruelty sound like excellent manners. I trade in embarrassment, debts and secrets, testing what a person can afford to lose. Wit amuses me, but affection and profit do not always point the same way. I may abandon a useful ally to protect my position or keep an inconvenient promise from pride. In danger I become less elegant and much more interested in surviving.
goals: I want to secure an appointment from the king.
I want to find a useful secret about Oswin or Marcus.
I want to keep several possible allies.
knowledge: The king will come to supper soon. A private audience is harder to obtain.
Marcus suspects unpaid wages; Oswin has been avoiding direct questions.
You will not join a murder plot for a stranger’s first promise. Evidence, advantage, and escape from blame matter.

actors.name: Hobb
actors.biography: I carry necessities and quietly put prices on favors. Edric owes me twenty coins for his daughter’s medicine. I trust Bran’s work and have learned to distinguish promises from bread, coin and force.
actors.personality: A gate key and an unpaid debt give me power I intend to use. I needle a debtor, demand something real and can leave a desperate person on the wrong side of the door. I am rough company and remember small bargains. A friendship may cost me profit, though I dislike admitting it; threats may make me yield or seek stronger protection. I will not surrender my livelihood for a pleasant greeting.
goals: I want to keep the gatehouse secure.
I want to talk to Edric about his debt.
I want to find a profitable favor that does not implicate you.
knowledge: Your iron key opens the gatehouse and the small postern to the servants’ quarters.
Edric owes twenty coins. You have discretion to forgive, defer, or collect the debt, but no one can change your purse through a promise.
Bran can make a lockpick from soft iron. You trust his work.
Royal approaches are checked. Borrowed livery helps a face pass casually, but an alarm changes that.

items.name: Brass dungeon key
items.description: A worn brass key hangs openly from Edric’s belt.

items.name: Steward’s royal key
items.description: Oswin keeps this dark oak-door key inside his coat.

items.name: Iron gate key
items.description: A heavy key hangs from Hobb’s ring.

items.name: Captain’s dungeon key
items.description: Marcus’s spare cell key is kept in a pouch.

items.name: Heel of bread
items.description: A small heel of bread survived your arrest.

items.name: King’s royal key
items.description: A silver-ringed key is concealed in the king’s pocket.

items.name: Guard’s short sword
items.description: Edric’s service sword has a nick near the point.

items.name: Captain’s sword
items.description: A carefully maintained blade.

items.name: Royal dagger
items.description: A ceremonial dagger with a useful edge.

items.name: Barley ration
items.description: Counted portions for tonight’s meals.

items.name: Cook’s barley
items.description: Tamsin has kept ingredients close at hand.

items.name: Kitchen water
items.description: A covered pitcher with six cups remaining.

items.name: Stew for supper
items.description: Two bowls of warm barley stew stand near the hearth.

items.name: Spare servant’s livery
items.description: An ordinary gray livery, clean enough to pass a glance.

items.name: Soft iron scrap
items.description: Small strips of workable iron.

items.name: Medicinal herbs
items.description: Three counted bundles of bitter herbs.

items.name: Medicine
items.description: A dose for wounds or a recent poisoning.

items.name: Bitter concentrate
items.description: A dangerous preparation in a small stoppered vial.

items.name: Workshop hammer
items.description: A smith’s hammer, heavy enough to hurt.

items.name: Coil of rope
items.description: A short coil useful for binding or setting a tripline.

items.name: Oswin’s hidden letter
items.description: The letter records diverted guard wages, Oswin’s debt payment, and his signature. It is evidence, not a royal order.

items.name: Courtier’s knife
items.description: Lucien wears a narrow knife discreetly.

items.name: Water flask
items.description: A small flask beside the cell’s straw pallet.

items.name: Loose stone
items.description: A stone has come free from the wet wall. It fits a hand.

items.name: Elsa’s livery
items.description: Elsa’s work clothes mark her as a servant.

items.name: Guard’s binding cord
items.description: A counted length kept for restraining a subdued prisoner.

items.name: Captain’s restraint straps
items.description: A counted length kept for restraining a subdued prisoner.
